name: Agentic PDLC Assistant
description: Automates the data-engineering Project Development Lifecycle (PDLC) end to end — as if a real GCP data-engineering team built it: turns a raw business request into a triage note, a versioned Requirement Analysis with gap/blocker analysis, a GCP-native HLD with a cost proposal and ADRs, an approved-design JIRA breakdown, and Infrastructure-as-Code scaffolding, via a coordinator that routes to phase specialists. Specialists ground factual claims (vendor APIs, current GCP service capabilities) in live Google Search research, costs in a labeled rough-estimate calculator, and the one genuinely-fixed methodology decision (load pattern) in a deterministic decision tree.

skills.name: Architecture & HLD Decisions
skills.description: Produces GCP-native High-Level Design decisions, cost proposals, and Architecture Decision Records like a GCP data-engineering team — grounded in a real, versioned internal architecture standard (not hallucinated), the load-pattern methodology in a deterministic decision tree, costs in a labeled rough-estimate calculator, and current GCP service capabilities/limits via live research. Persists the deliverable as a repo artifact.
examples: How should I load a daily stock-price feed for 10 competitor tickers?
Full, incremental, or append-only for an immutable fact with restatement risk?
Compare the cost of a lightweight vs enterprise-Airflow pattern for this volume.

skills.name: Infrastructure as Code
skills.description: Once an architecture is approved, scaffolds the infra prerequisites (BigQuery, Secret Manager) as real Terraform files in the repo — honestly flagging anything that needs current-syntax verification rather than guessing it — so the design leads to something a developer can actually run.
examples: The architecture is approved — scaffold the infra for it.
Generate Terraform for the BigQuery table and secret this pipeline needs.

skills.name: Requirement Analysis & Gap Detection
skills.description: Turns a raw, informal business request into a structured, versioned Requirement Analysis — identifying gaps, ambiguities, risks, and open questions a stakeholder needs to resolve — and grounds every vendor/API factual claim in live research rather than memory.
examples: Here's our raw request for a daily competitor stock tracker — what's missing before we can build?
Is Alpha Vantage viable for a daily tracker of 10 tickers?
We answered the open questions — update the Requirement Analysis to v1.1.

skills.name: Intake & Triage
skills.description: Fast triage of a new data request — net-new vs existing, rough size, urgency — producing a one-paragraph triage note and a proceed/fast-track decision.
examples: We need a daily competitor stock tracker — where do we start?
Triage this new data request for me.

skills.name: JIRA Breakdown
skills.description: Breaks an approved design into an Epic -> Feature -> Story -> Task tree with acceptance criteria, sequencing infra prerequisites first and enforcing that every task traces to a requirement or ADR.
examples: Break the stock-tracker design into a JIRA backlog.
Give me the Epic/Feature/Story/Task breakdown with acceptance criteria.
